transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-18
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alyssa (Redwood AE), Marcus (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood CSM), Raj (Valleyview Head of AI), Karen (Platform Eng), Marta (Security), Liam (Product)

Summary:
Quick onboarding kickoff for Valleyview Health's Redwood deployment. Discussed onboarding plan, timelines for test VPC, SSO/SAML, data residency, and next steps for private vs hosted evaluation. Agreed to run a small pilot in our dedicated environment then evaluate private deployment options for PHI workloads.

00:00 Raj: All right I think we can start, yeah thanks everyone for joining, uh this is Raj from Valleyview. We're excited to kick off the Redwood onboarding.
00:05 Alyssa: Hi Raj, hi team, thanks for the time. I'm Alyssa, I'll be your AE and point of contact for the kickoff. Marcus is our SE and will handle the technical runbook, and Priya on CSM side to help with onboarding and success.
00:12 Marcus: Hey everyone, quick intro, Marcus Lee, SE. I'll walk through the technical tasks and the private deployment checklist later in the call.
00:18 Karen: Great thanks. Quick note, we have to make sure anything touching PHI is isolated, okay. Marta is here for security questions.
00:25 Marta: Yep thanks, uh, hi. We'll need SOC2 details, encryption at rest and in transit, and KMS integration. Also need to know about audit logs and retention.
00:35 Alyssa: Absolutely, we have a security packet, I'll share the SOC2 and ISO docs. For KMS we support customer-managed keys and HSM integrations, details in the security pack.
00:44 Marcus: Just to set expectations, most customers start on hosted Redwood to get immediate value and then move to dedicated or private for PHI. For onboarding, we'll do test workloads in a sandbox, run throughput tests, then if you need, we schedule the private deployment.
00:58 Liam: Timeline-wise we want a pilot within two weeks-ish, and then a production plan by end of month if everything looks good. Is that feasible?
01:05 Marcus: Two weeks for a pilot is realistic — provided the VPC and access are ready. If you go hosted we can start even quicker, like within 48 hours.
01:12 Raj: We prefer private for PHI but can do initial eval on hosted to speed up. Can we ensure no data persists beyond session for hosted eval?
01:20 Priya: For hosted evals we can configure data retention and opt-out of logging on the test endpoints, and we also have an NDA/DPAs to cover that. I'll attach the DPA.
01:30 Marta: We need confirmation on data residency and how logs are stored. Also SAML SSO integration is required for our engineers, and RBAC.
01:37 Alyssa: We support SAML/SSO and SCIM provisioning. I'll send the SAML metadata examples. RBAC is configurable in Console with roles for engineers, read-only for auditors, etc.
01:48 Karen: Network question — for private deployment do you require inbound rules? Or is it outbound only via the customer's NAT?
01:55 Marcus: For our private deployment we usually require customer-provided networking: a VPC with private subnets for the inference nodes. Outbound egress is limited and we can provide a list of IP ranges to allow. We don't require inbound ports open to the internet.
02:08 Raj: Great. Also on the model side, we have two workloads: a consumer-facing summarization and an internal clinical note extraction that touches PHI. We need latency SLOs for the consumer path (200-300ms) and throughput for bulk extraction. How do we set that?
02:20 Marcus: Those are common patterns. For low latency you may want dedicated capacity with optimized quantized models; we can recommend model and quantization profiles per workload. For batch extraction we can configure autoscaling and batching. We'll run a baseline benchmark during the pilot and provide per-token latency breakdowns in the Console.
02:36 Liam: Will we be able to see token-level cost and performance on per-route dashboards?
02:40 Marcus: Yeah the Console shows per-route cost, token counts, latency percentiles. We'll show you where the cost levers are — batching, cache, and model selection.
02:48 Marta: Encryption — at rest must be customer-managed KMS. Also for logs we need an audit log stream to our SIEM. Is syslog or S3 push supported?
02:57 Alyssa: We support KMS for encryption-at-rest, and audit logs can be exported to your S3 or pushed to SIEM. We'll include log export options in the runbook.
03:06 Raj: On the legal side, procurement hopes to get pricing and contract by next week. Who's the contact?
03:10 Alyssa: I'll follow up with pricing and contract contacts after this call. I'll also include our standard onboarding checklist and timeline.
03:17 Karen: For the pilot we'll need sample prompts and a dataset for the extraction test. Is Redwood able to run the benchmark on our dataset behind our VPC?
03:25 Marcus: Yes, we can run benchmarks in your VPC for the private pilot. We'll also replicate the same tests in hosted for apples-to-apples comparison. We'll need a small sample dataset and expected outputs.
03:34 Raj: Security question again — do you support bring-your-own-model or are we limited to Redwood-curated models? We have some internal fine-tuned variants we want to serve.
03:42 Marcus: On private deployments you can bring your own model artifacts, yes. On hosted we can support loading customer models with additional compliance review; the common path is to start with Redwood-curated verified models then bring models to private.
03:53 Marta: About rollouts and fallback — if the private cluster can't handle spikes, is there an automatic fallback to hosted? And how is data routed?
04:01 Marcus: We have smart routing policies — can route by latency, cost, or region. Fallbacks to hosted are possible but require data residency and compliance alignment. For PHI you generally keep everything private and use reserved capacity with bursting options.
04:14 Liam: Are there any common gotchas for onboarding tile? e.g., firewall configs, certs, etc?
04:19 Marcus: Yeah the main blockers are: 1) missing egress rules for our provded IP range, 2) not sharing SAML metadata early, 3) model artifact packaging differences for BYOM. We'll put these in the checklist.
04:30 Priya: On CSM side, I'll run weekly check-ins during the pilot and make sure we're hitting your success criteria. Let's define success criteria now — Raj?
04:36 Raj: For the pilot: 1) <300ms p95 for consumer route, 2) >=95% extraction accuracy on our sample set, 3) no PHI leakage in logs, 4) complete runbook and IaC for private deploy.
04:49 Priya: Perfect, we'll track those.
04:52 Karen: Can we get a quick demo of the Console later? Just to see dashboards and rollout controls.
04:57 Alyssa: Yes we can schedule a short demo. Marcus can do a focused Console walk-through. How's next Wednesday for 30 minutes?
05:05 Raj: Works for us.
05:07 Marta: One more on compliance — does Redwood's private deployment have SOC2 and is the audit report shareable?
05:12 Alyssa: Redwood has SOC2 and ISO, and the report is shareable under NDA. I'll drop the security packet and the SOC2 summary.
05:20 Liam: Pricing — can you give a rough estimate for dedicated capacity for our expected load? We'll share expected qps.
05:26 Alyssa: If you share expected qps and sequence lengths we'll put together a cost estimate. For now I'll provide a ballpark for a reserved starter pool and options for burst capacity.
05:35 Raj: Ok that sounds good. Anything else we should cover?
05:38 Marcus: I'll run through immediate technical deliverables: network IP ranges, SAML metadata example, model packaging doc, and private deploy runbook.
05:45 Alyssa: I'll send the onboarding checklist, pricing contact, DPA, and the security packet. Priya will set up weekly cadence.
05:52 Priya: I'll create a calendar invite for weekly check-ins and the Console demo next Wednesday. Also setting up a shared Slack channel.
05:59 Raj: Great thanks everyone. Quick recap of next steps?
06:02 Alyssa: Recap: 1) Alyssa send onboarding checklist + security docs + pricing contact. 2) Marcus share networking IP ranges, runbook, and model packaging. 3) Valleyview to provision test VPC and share SAML metadata and sample dataset. 4) Priya to schedule weekly check-ins and Console demo.
06:20 Raj: Perfect. Thanks all, we'll follow up in Slack and email.
06:24 Meeting end.
